- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.4) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) and price is trending up, cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high to avoid false optimism.
- For 30-day horizons, if last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price dropping after spike), model should adjust downward by 2–5% in next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and price is volatile, reduce forecast variance by 10–15% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
- If forecast consistently overestimates true price by >3% over 3–5 days, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for the next 3–5 days.
- For sentiment history with repeated small up/down swings (e.g., 0.18, 0.36, -0.08), model should smooth out 3–5 day forecast peaks and troughs by 1–3% to avoid overreacting to sentiment noise.
